stories.title: Why Wasn't The Cook "Fumble" NOT a Rams Penalty?
stories.summary:
Cook was clearly punched also with the ball.  There was no act of "stripping"... No interpretation.



	 



	Why isn't the "Peanut Punch" being penalized?  It's illegal to use the technique even more illegal when the player ends up missing and  also hitting the player in possession of the ball, which happened on the Cook play. 



	 



	Why is Cook being faulted here.  It's a clearly illegal technique the NFL is refusing to enforce.



	 



	"Punching the ball is illegal in football when a player is in possession of it, but officials are instructed to assume a defender is legally stripping the ball if there is any doubt. If a defender misses the ball and punches a player instead, it would be penalized as striking under Rule 12.  Punching the Ball: A player cannot punch or bat a ball that is NOT in their possession. This is considered illegal."

stories.title: The True Defensive Bugaboo
stories.summary:
TEXANS



	Red Zone: 4/5



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	LIONS 



	Red Zone: 3/4



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	CHARGERS 



	Red Zone: 1/4



	4th Down: 0/1



	 



	PATRIOTS



	Red Zone: 3/3



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	RAMS



	Red Zone: 5/5



	4th Down: 2/2



	 



	Through 4 games:



	Opponents have score a TD in the red zone 76% of the time: 16/21, good for 27th in the league. Doesn’t matter if the opposing offense was previously struggling in that area, the Bills defense is the cure all.



	 



	Opponents have converted 4th downs 88% of the time: 8/9, good for 29th in the league.



	 



	These numbers HAVE to start regressing to the mean at some point. The Bills can’t be this putrid against every contender, can they? If those numbers can get to at least middle of the pack, I’d wager we all would feel very different about Jim Leonhard and his defense.

stories.title: Brandon Beane vs. Les Snead
stories.summary:
The Bills walked out of Sofi with a W last night solely on the back of Josh Allen and maybe James Cook, but it was kinda frightening watching that game at time.   For a portion of it it looked like a JV vs. Varsity team.   A lot of people are hating on Jim Leonard right now for seemingly somehow making the defense worse this season.   From my eyes most of their weakness really just comes down to talent mismatches in a lot of areas.   



	 



	The two GMs of these teams seem to have polar opposite approaches to team building.   Everyone was talking about how the Rams were mortgaging their future back in 2021 when they traded for Stafford and Von Miller but despite a setback in 2022 they've stayed just as competitive as the Bills in recent years while arguably being in a tougher division.   In 2025 They went out and signed Davante Adams for a 2 year $46,000,000 deal, some were calling that an overpay for a washed aging vet.   Just this season they "mortgaged their future" again by trading for Myles Garrett and Trent Mcduffie.   For Garrett they gave up Jared Verse, a 1st, 2nd, 3rd rd. pick AND are paying him a 5 year $208,000,000 contract.    For McDuffie they gave up another 1st and a 6th rd pick AND are paying him roughly $31,000,000 AAV.   Les Snead and the Rams clearly want to go after proven elite talent at key positions and don't seem to care the cost.   



	 



	Perhaps their high risk gambles will finally catch up to them but currently they are rostering 7 different All Pro players and chasing their 2nd ring in 6 years.  



	 



	 



	Beane's approach to team building is a more frugal, promote from within, draft for depth, never pay top dollar for outside talent with a little mix of just throwing sh*t at the wall to see what sticks.  He likes to re-sign and often overpay his own players(Bernard, Oliver, Knox), overpay for mid tier players(Palmer, Samuel) and then panic sign even more players when there is clear talent deficiencies at positons(Amari Cooper, Brandon Cooks, etc.).   Despite Beane's reluctance to pay for elite talent(He was hesitant on even giving James cook a new contract), the Bills are near bottom of the league in available cap space the next few years.   Outside of Josh Allen and (Ray Davis? lol) the Bills are rostering zero All Pros.   



	 



	You could make a case that Beane's approach is the better option since the Bills do have better overall record of 70-32 over the last 5 years vs. the Rams 58-41 but LA has made deeper playoff runs and a ring and despite always mortgaging their future on blockbuster trades they keep hanging around.   



	 



	My personal opinion is I would like to see a happy medium between these two GMs.   I would like to see Beane be more aggressive about bringing in elite talent at skill positions without going full Les Snead and trading away three 1st round picks.   I would also like him to bring in more outside talent instead of resigning guys like Terell Bernard just because he's homegrown.   Building your team for depth seems nice but you tend to get bullied when you play other elite teams.   Beane also needs to bring in a coach that has ties to the Shanahan tree.   The Bills seriously need help in running a more efficient timing based passing offense.   It should not be that hard to have a 3 step drop and get the ball out to an open receiver.   Either Josh isn't reading the field properly or guys aren't getting schemed open well enough.   In either case, they need help.

stories.title: Hey, I just looked outside. The sky isn't falling. We are 4-1
stories.summary:
Look, I will admit right off the bat that it hasn't been pretty the last 3 weeks and the defense has been horrible throughout most of the 5 games. 



	 



	But we are 4-1. I'm pretty sure at the beginning of the year if we were told that would be the case we would have jumped on that. And we are tied as the #1 scoring offense in the NFL. And that's been by and large without DJ Moore who changes everything when he is out there. 



	 



	I will freely admit our defense is terrible outside the DL. But we are still stacking wins. 



	 



	Sure, it's ugly at times. And there is a LOT of work to do on defense especially. But there's a lot to like on this team right now as well. We have a good DL. Two full fledged stars there in Groot and Walker. And Carter is right behind them. Benford actually looked better last night and, considering the assignment, IGB played well I thought. 



	 



	It's October. Just keep stacking wins. Find a way to contain Bowers next week and 5-1 heading in to the bye is attainable.

stories.title: The Beane Era Needs To End
stories.summary: Something about this game has pushed my tolerance level of Beane over the edge.  This game looked like Josh Allen against the Rams.  The defense was Swiss Cheese the entire night, and the Rams man coverage blanketed our receivers for much of the game - forcing Josh to put on his cape and make some crazy plays with his legs.  Yes, we won, but it was like a nightmarish repeat of everything this team does that comes up short when the playoffs come around.  At the end of the 4th Quarter, how many of you were yelling at the screen - "Just let them score so we have 40 seconds left."  That's not a good way to think about the team's defense.  😆  I hope it's something to do with the coaching, but I'm seeing a lot of gaps in talent on this team.  A lot.  And it feels like Beane has made some more whiffs on picks.

James Cook  - You hate him, you love him
stories.summary:
1st play of the game, he fumbled. Now you remember he fumbled in Houston game (we recovered). He fumbled in the Denver playoff game, which was still a turning point of the game for me.



	 



	But despite his goofy, indifferent appearance, he does care. You see he cheered the defense making a stop. And then he just took over late 4th quarter, pretty much the main force to get the Bills the lead and expand the lead, as well as a minor icing of the game.



	 



	He's 27. I'm not sure he's going to change. We can't live with him on those mistakes, but we also can't live without him to drive the offense, sort of what we had with Allen before he matured. 



	 



	 BTW, James, please have both hands on the ball the last few carries you had - I just don't like to hold on my breath too much in those situations.
